shortlist: Acute dacryocystitis with secondary optic nerve injury

selector.runner_up: Acute dacryocystitis with secondary optic nerve injury
selector.rationale: Imaging studies show left-sided lacrimal sac abscess and postseptal fat stranding, with cultures isolating Streptococcus pyogenes, which best explains the patient's presentation

rejected.label: Orbital cellulitis
rejected.why: While there is evidence of edema and hyperemia, the primary issue appears to be localized to the lacrimal sac

rejected.label: Optic neuritis
rejected.why: The optic nerve injury is secondary to the lacrimal sac abscess, as evidenced by diffusion-weighted imaging showing acute injury to the orbital segment of the left optic nerve

rejected.label: Dacryocystitis
rejected.why: Dacryocystitis is a broader term that encompasses lacrimal sac abscess, but the specific diagnosis of lacrimal sac abscess is more precise
